summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and Polaris Cloud to explore partner integration for GPU-enabled dedicated/private deployment, go-to-market motion, and technical requirements. Polaris is interested in hosting Redwood Dedicated on their managed GPU offering and embedding Redwood API for managed customers. Key topics: deployment topologies (VPC, on-prem), KMS/tenant isolation, billing/commissions, SSO, and next steps to run a tech deep dive and share benchmarks.
topics: Partner integration models (managed offering vs resell)
Deployment modes: Dedicated vs Private/VPC vs On-prem
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Menon (Redwood SE); Amina Rahman (Polaris Head of Partnerships); Carlos Vega (Polaris Solutions Architect); Leah Kim (Polaris Sales Eng)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): All right, folks, thanks for carving out time. Jordan from Redwood here, AE on the account. Priya's our solutions lead, she'll cover the tech bits. Amina — thanks for organizing.
[00:08] Amina (Polaris): Yeah, thanks, Jordan. Really excited to chat. We run a managed GPU infra service and curious about a partner model — embed Redwood for our customers and also offer Dedicated deployments.
[00:16] Priya (Redwood): Hi everyone. Quick agenda: 1) understand Polaris' business model and customer patterns; 2) walk through integration options (hosted API vs dedicated pools vs private deployments in your VPC); 3) security/compliance checklist; 4) next steps. Sound OK?
[00:28] Carlos (Polaris): Yep, sounds good. I'll briefly sketch our infra and typical SLAs so you can react.
[00:35] Leah (Polaris): And I'm mostly focused on go-to-market mechanics and how billing works if we resell.
[00:40] Jordan: Perfect. Carlos, over to you.
[00:45] Carlos: Quick context: Polaris manages racks in multiple regions, we expose managed GPU instances to customers (NVidia A100, H200 in our fleet). Typical customers are fintechs and health startups — they need both low latency and compliance. We currently run k8s with metalLB and some custom node provisioning. We do offer private tenancy right now but want to add ML inference partners.
[01:05] Priya: Super helpful. When you say private tenancy, is that single-tenant VPC per customer or multi-tenant with network isolation?
[01:12] Carlos: Mostly single-tenant VPCs for enterprise customers. For smaller customers, we spin up isolated namespaces. For partner integrations we'd prefer offering two options: 1) embed Redwood-hosted API as a managed endpoint for smaller customers, 2) provide Redwood Dedicated inside our infra for larger customers who want predictable throughput.
[01:32] Jordan: That matches common asks. On the Dedicated side we can provision reserved GPU pools and expose an API that routes to the Dedicated cluster. For Private it's possible to run our control plane on our side with a customer-managed runtime — basically Redwood Private deployed into your VPC.
[01:47] Amina: What's the difference from a compliance perspective between Dedicated and Private?
[01:52] Priya: Good question. Dedicated is still a Redwood-managed environment but with reserved capacity — data isolation at the tenant level, encryption in transit and at rest. Private means we hand you a customer-managed control plane or we install in your VPC so you own the keys and network. For SOC2/ISO customers, Private gives the strongest control and auditability.
[02:12] Leah: And KMS — can we use our HSM or cloud KMS?
[02:16] Priya: Yes, KMS integration is supported. For Private we can integrate your cloud KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we support customer KMS in certain models — we'll need a quick security review.
[02:26] Carlos: Ok. On perf — our ops team cares about token throughput and sequence lengths. Do you have public benchmarks we can look at?
[02:32] Jordan: We do. I'll share the benchmark spreadsheet for representative models and token lengths. Priya, can you comment on kernel selection and GPU mapping for H200 vs A100?
[02:40] Priya: Sure. Short answer: model architecture and quantization profile drive kernel choices. For shorter sequences and chat workloads the memory/KV cache patterns matter. H200 has advantages on some LLM ops; A100 is very solid for throughput in older models. We'll propose a mapping: small models on 1xA100 or 1xH200; larger gen models use 2x or multi-GPU partitioning depending on sequence length. We'll include latency vs cost tradeoffs in the doc.
[03:05] Amina: Do you support continuous batching and prefix caching? Some of our customers care about tail latency more than average.
[03:13] Priya: Yes, continuous batching and KV/prefix caching are core to our runtime. We can tune batching windows per tenant to ensure latency SLOs are met; there's always a tradeoff with cost.
[03:24] Leah: On the GTM side: if we're reselling Redwood Dedicated or embedding the API for our dashboard, how does billing and commissions work?
[03:32] Jordan: There are a few models: referral fee, reseller margin, or co-sell with a committed discount. For Dedicated/resell we usually do monthly reserved capacity contracts and then pass through usage or meter internally. We'd need to align on billing flow — whether Polaris invoices customers and pays Redwood, or Redwood invoices customers directly via whitelabel. We can share partner pricing options.
[03:55] Amina: Good. I also need to check with legal on partner terms — is there a standard partner agreement?
[03:59] Jordan: Yes, we have a partner program pack — I'll attach it. Should include NDA, partner reseller terms, and an MSA for larger deals.
[04:10] Carlos: On the deeper infra side: how intrusive is Redwood Private to deploy in our environment? We run a controlled air-gapped cluster for some customers.
[04:18] Priya: For Private we provide a deployable control plane, Helm charts, and installers. Air-gapped installs are supported but we typically need an initial connectivity window for licensing and metrics; we can work around that with offline licensing tokens. We'll prepare a sample Helm chart and the infra spec.
[04:36] Leah: How are service updates handled in Private — do you push updates or does Polaris maintain them?
[04:41] Priya: There are two modes: managed Private where Redwood ops handles upgrades under a scheduled maintenance window, and self-managed where Polaris runs the control plane and we provide versioned artifacts and upgrade notes.
[04:51] Carlos: Do you support model rollouts and canarying? We want to be able to control model versions at a per-tenant level.
[04:57] Priya: Absolutely — rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies are built into Redwood. You can pin tenants to model versions or use traffic-splitting rules.
[05:06] Amina: Are there any known limitations with multi-tenant networks or with MetalLB?
[05:11] Priya: Not specifically; we integrate with standard k8s networking. MetalLB is fine. We do recommend certain CNI and load balancer patterns for predictable egress IPs for allowlist purposes. We'll include our recommended network topology.
[05:25] Jordan: Quick note — partners often ask about observability. Our Console provides per-route latency and cost breakdowns, token-level sampling, and tracing hooks so your support team can debug customer issues.
[05:36] Leah: Important for our support flow. Also curious if you have prebuilt connectors (e.g., Salesforce, Zendesk) or is that on the roadmap?
[05:44] Jordan: The Redwood Console focuses on inferencing observability; we do ship SDKs and some reference connectors. Integrations like Salesforce typically live in customer apps, but we can help with a reference integration pattern.
[05:55] Carlos: Security checks — SSO/SAML and RBAC. We need SAML for our portal so customers get single sign-on into the management UI.
[06:02] Priya: SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for the Console and can map to tenant-level RBAC. For Private we can plug into your IdP as well.
[06:12] Amina: For customers in EU healthcare, data residency matters. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
[06:18] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is supported — you can pin workloads to specific regions and we can advise on data residency patterns for logs and telemetry. For Private, since control plane lives in your VPC, residency is under your control.
[06:30] Leah: Are there any integration SDKs you recommend for partner embedding? We want to show a demo to customers from our dashboard.
[06:36] Jordan: JS and Python SDKs are our most used. We also support REST. For embedding in a dashboard, a proxy pattern combined with per-customer API keys works well. We can share a short demo snippet.
[06:48] Carlos: On lifecycle: how do model updates and quantization recommendations get rolled out? If a customer wants quantized models for cost, how do we validate quality?
[06:56] Priya: We have Redwood Optimize which suggests quantization profiles and model variants. We also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals so you can detect regressions. For partner deployments we can run joint evals on representative prompts before recommending a rollout.
[07:12] Amina: Great. Any concerns around IP or data retention for partner-resold customers?
[07:17] Jordan: We support configurable retention windows and can disable data retention for customers who need it. IP is the customer's — we don't claim rights. We'll put that in the partner docs.
[07:28] Leah: How about latency SLOs — can you commit to p50/p95 metrics for Dedicated inside our infra?
[07:35] Priya: We set latency SLOs based on model selection and batching windows. For Dedicated, with reserved pools and tuned batching, hitting p95 under target is typical; exact numbers depend on token lengths. We'll map sample p50/p95 in the benchmark spreadsheet we'll send.
[07:52] Carlos: Do you support auto-scaling for Dedicated pools if a customer spikes?
[07:56] Jordan: Yes, autoscaling policies and burst capacity are options — with some lead time for reserved resources. For partners wanting predictable billing, burst capacity can be metered.
[08:06] Amina: On commercials again — for a partner who wants to white-label, do you offer an OEM or white-label contract?
[08:12] Jordan: We have reseller and OEM-style agreements for larger partners. The partner pack has details. For early pilots we usually do a simple referral/reseller setup and then move to OEM as revenue scales.
[08:25] Leah: For pilots, what's the typical onboarding timeline?
[08:28] Priya: For hosted API pilots it can be days. For Dedicated pilot (reserved GPUs) we recommend 2–4 weeks to provision and tune. Private deployments can take 4–8 weeks depending on air-gap and compliance needs.
[08:42] Carlos: Ok, sounds reasonable. Let's talk about a proof-of-concept: we have a mid-market customer looking for low-latency chat with 4k context. Would Redwood be able to run a Dedicated pool and we can test with their traffic?
[08:54] Priya: Yes — that's a typical POC. We can provision a Dedicated pool mapped to 4k context models, enable KV caching, and run a short benchmark. We'll want sample prompts and traffic profiles.
[09:05] Jordan: Action item — we'll send a POC checklist and benchmark template.
[09:09] Amina: On the partner enablement side — we need collateral and a quick training for our sales engineers. Do you do partner training?
[09:17] Jordan: Yes, we do a short partner enablement session — usually 60–90 minutes covering product, integrations, and runbooks. We'll schedule one after we share the deck.
[09:27] Leah: Also, support SLAs — if one of our customers hits an incident, how do support handoffs work?
[09:32] Priya: We recommend a triage playbook: initial contact via Polaris support, escalation to Redwood's partner support with a tag, and joint incident bridge if needed. For Dedicated/Paid tiers we provide 24/7 support options.
[09:46] Carlos: Any specific network ports or egress allowlists we need to know for Private?
[09:51] Priya: We'll share a network requirements doc. Generally we need outbound to Redwood artifact repos for initial install (unless air-gapped), and control plane endpoints for license and metrics.
[09:59] Jordan: Quick check — is Polaris more interested in Resell (you bill end customers) or Managed (we bill) in the near-term?
[10:05] Amina: For speed to market, resell with referral sounds easiest. Long-term we want a managed Dedicated option embedded in our portal.
[10:13] Jordan: Good — we'll propose a starter reseller flow and a timeline for a Dedicated pilot.
[10:18] Leah: One more on metrics — do you expose per-tenant cost estimators so we can show customers expected costs?
[10:24] Priya: Yes, the Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost estimators. We can share sample dashboards.
[10:31] Carlos: Any compatibility issues with your runtime and our GPU drivers or kernel versions?
[10:36] Priya: We publish supported driver versions and kernel matrices. There's usually a small matrix of tested drivers for A100 and H200. We'll include that.
[10:46] Amina: OK, time check — about 35 more minutes; maybe we should call out explicit next steps and owners.
[10:54] Jordan: Agreed. Quick recap then action items. Recap: 1) Polaris exploring reseller + Dedicated; 2) Redwood can support Dedicated and Private installs with KMS/SSO; 3) need benchmarks and POC checklist; 4) partner pack + legal.
[11:10] Amina: Sounds right. I'll confirm internal stakeholders and share the list.
[11:15] Jordan: Action items: we'll send partner deck, benchmark sheet, sample Helm chart, and schedule SE deep dive. Priya anything to add?
[11:23] Priya: I'll prepare infra spec and note driver/kernel compatibility and private install notes.
[11:29] Carlos: I'll send target customer use cases and expected p95 targets.
[11:33] Leah: I'll coordinate scheduling for enablement and our pilot customer.
[11:37] Jordan: Great. Last question — any competitors you're evaluating that we should be aware of?
[11:42] Amina: Mainly PicoServe and BigCloud AI. We're also exploring a homegrown inference stack but that has slower time-to-market.
[11:50] Jordan: Thanks — that helps with positioning. Anything else from the Polaris side?
[11:54] Carlos: No, that's it.
[11:56] Jordan: OK we'll follow up with the materials by Monday (2025-09-15). Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[11:59] Amina: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains natural speech patterns and occasional overlaps; some product names abbreviated in the recording (e.g., 'K-V cash' transcription artifacts).
